messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — GPU allocation failures in account prod-42 / region us-east-2. Autoscaler unable to attach new instances (ServiceLimitExceeded). Severity: P1. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4400001111

matt (oncall): I'm on it, paging infra + cs. Starting investigation.

sanjay: seeing repeated errors in autoscaler: 
```
2026-03-17T14:02:04Z ERROR attach: Request was denied by AWS: ServiceLimitExceeded: You have requested more accelerators than your quota allows.
ResourceType: gpu.p4d, requested: 8, available: 0
```

elena (infra): confirming: account-level accelerator quota is at hard cap. No new ENI/attach allowed. Looks like account hit a soft cap that is now enforced.

rob-cs: customer impact: Support is reporting 3 customers with 429s on model-inference routes, one enterprise (ACME Corp) saying high-latency on critical endpoints. Preparing comms.

matt (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) Reroute affected traffic to other regions with spare capacity, 2) Fallback low-priority workloads to cpu-quantized variant, 3) Throttle non-critical tenants. Which is fastest?

sanjay: I can push a cross-region routing override for the list of affected projects in 2-3 mins (us-east-2 -> us-east-1). Will also flip model-fallback for queued low-priority jobs.

elena (infra): please do routing override. I'm opening AWS support case and requesting rapid quota bump. Case ID: 1234567890. Tagging TAM.

liz-ops: enabling tenant-level throttles for background batch jobs now so foreground traffic has headroom. Patch rolling: /api/v1/overrides -> set priority.threshold=high for prod lanes.

matt (oncall): applying route override now for projects: prod-42, prod-88, edge-test-3. Will monitor queue length.

sanjay: route override applied. New requests should go to us-east-1. Backlog drain started.

incident-bot: UPDATE — Routing override applied by matt (oncall) at 14:06 UTC. Autoscaler attachments still failing in us-east-2.

rob-cs: Sent initial customer notice to ACME (they acknowledged). Internal status page updated.

elena (infra): AWS support responded: case 1234567890 in progress; requested justification and spike window. They've provisionally increased soft limit after TAM approval but final quota change will take ~45-90 mins.

sanjay: meanwhile I've toggled model fallback for non-SLA queues: using small-quantized variant (cpu) as fallback. Reduces GPU demand by ~60%.

matt (oncall): Good. Keeping high-priority production traffic on GPU but routed to us-east-1. Low-priority jobs on fallback. Any observed error rate improvements?

liz-ops: 429 counts for affected routes down 75% after reroute + throttles. Latency for routed requests in us-east-1 stable. Backlog in us-east-2 queue is draining slowly (~120 jobs left).

elena (infra): confirm AWS support updated quota provisionally; still need post-change verification. I'm preparing runbook steps for postmortem and capacity plan (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-quota-escalation).

incident-bot: NOTE — Post-incident actions queued: request reserved capacity for prod-42, update autoscaler to prefer multi-region warm pools, add stronger preflight quota checks to deploy pipeline.

matt (oncall): Handing off to elena + ops for follow-up. I'll move this thread to #postmortems for RCA after quota is fully resolved. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:

rob-cs: I'll follow up with customers and send ETA when AWS confirms final quota increase.

aws-support-bot: Case 1234567890 updated: provisional increase applied + TAM contact assigned. Final quota change ETA ~00:50:00.

elena (infra): adding this to oncall handoff: monitor for 2 hours post-apply, validate autoscaler can successfully attach new instances, and confirm no residual failovers.

matt (oncall): last update before handoff: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced, waiting on AWS final. Handoff time 14:22 UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Handoff complete.
